text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty: HIGH - service: infer-queue-capacity-exhaustion triggered (policy: queue_backlog > 3000 for 5m). PagerDuty incident: PD-4821

ada: paging oncall — I just saw PD-4821. queue backlog spiked to ~4.2k.

mohit: acked PD-4821. jumping in. seeing long tail on /v1/generate and many requests waiting in celery queue.

sarah: timeline? did anything deploy recently?

mohit: no deploys from prod-main in last 30m. metric dump: 
```
queue_length: 4208
consumer_replicas: 18
avg_latency_ms: 420
kv_cache_size_mb: 41200
cpu_util: 78%
gpu_util: 92%
```

ada: kv_cache_size 41GB?? that seems high. we had a bug where prefix caching didn't evict for certain long-running conversations.

ben: yikes. that could blow up memory and slow down inference if kv lookups are huge. are evictions disabled?

mohit: checking autoscaler logs now. looks like HPA target based on cpu only; gpu-backed pods not scaling because metrics-server isn't reporting gpu memory pressure. autoscaler didn't trigger burst capacity.

incident-bot: Related alert: autoscaler:scale-missed (3 failures in 10m).

ada: ok mitigation plan: 1) reduce incoming concurrency per route to shed load 2) enable fallback to smaller model for non-critical requests 3) manual scale up of dedicated pool / trigger burst from reserved capacity if available 4) investigate kv cache eviction fix.

sarah: can we immediately flip a route-level limiter? I can patch routing config to set concurrency_limit=1 for @public/generate for next 10m. that will raise client 429s but limit backlog.

mohit: do that. I'll prepare the fallback model rollout. use rdw-moderate-1 as fallback (half token cost).

ben: I'm ready to hit manual scale if you confirm which pool. this is hosted-dedicated-prod-us-east-1 pool A. we have reserved burst capacity of +6 GPUs.

ada: do manual scale and enable burst. comment the command here when you run it.

ben: running: 
```
# k8s command to scale inference group
kubectl scale deployment/infer-pool-a --replicas=24 -n prod-inference
# trigger reserved burst
rdwctl capacity-burst --pool prod-pool-a --add 6 --reason "PD-4821 kv-cache surge"
```

ben: done. replicas -> 24, burst requested. watching.

mohit: starting canary traffic switch to rdw-moderate-1 using routing weight: 10% -> 50% then 100%. patching now.

sarah: patched concurrency limiter on public route: concurrency=1, window=60s. clients will see throttling. :warning:

incident-bot: autoscaler:scale-success (manual scale detected)

mohit: canary at 10% now. latency for fallback model ~210ms, no failed requests so far.

ada: what's the effect on queue length?

mohit: queue_length dropping: 4208 -> 3100 -> 2100 in 6m. kv_cache_size still high but growth rate slowing.

ben: reserved burst allocation accepted, new GPUs reporting: 6 added, utilization dropping from 92% -> 65%.

sarah: suggestion: if kv cache holds stale prefixes, we can trigger a coordinated eviction on a subset of pods to avoid heavy cache rebuild. do we have a safe eviction command?

mohit: we do. plan: do rolling eviction on 25% of pods, wait 30s, verify latencies. command: 
```
curl -X POST "https://internal-api/prod/cache/evict?scope=prefix&percent=25" -H "Authorization: Bearer ${OP_TOKEN}"
```

ada: do it in 2 waves. I'm worried about regen traffic spike, but with fallback model and extra GPUs we should absorb it.

mohit: running wave 1 now.

mohit: wave1 evict returned 200. queue_length dipped further to 1400.

sarah: wave2 scheduled in 45s.

incident-bot: PD-4821 status update: acknowledged by mohit.

ben: heads-up: ops-alert from customer-success: 3 large customers reported slow responses and timeouts for 3–6 minutes earlier; no 5xx logged now.

ada: please log affected customers in PD ticket. include timeframe and that we applied fallback and burst.

mohit: wave2 done. kv_cache_size now 12GB (eviction effective). avg_latency_ms -> 180ms. queue_length 620.

sarah: removing concurrency limiter and gradually increasing routing weight back to original.

mohit: rollback canary: routing weight restored to 100% for main model; fallback set to standby.

ben: I'm keeping burst capacity pinned for 15m to absorb any replays.

incident-bot: PagerDuty: PD-4821 status changed to Resolved by mohit at 1729456910

ada: summary for postmortem: root cause = autoscaler not considering gpu memory/kv cache pressure + cache eviction bug that prevented pruning long prefixes. mitigation = manual scale + reserved burst + route-level concurrency limits + rolling cache eviction + fallback model. customer impact = transient slow responses for a subset of customers, no long-term data loss.

sarah: creating follow-up ticket to add gpu memory metric into HPA scaling signal and a guardrail to auto-evict if kv_cache > 30GB. tagging eng-runtime and eng-ml.

ben: handing off to night oncall @ben for 2h watch. set PD to low-alert. :white_check_mark:

ada: thanks team — nice quick mitigation. I'll open the postmortem draft. :thumbsup:
